Subscribe The Crown Prosecution Service asked a US court on Monday to keep Tristan Tate and Andrew Tate in jail while extradition proceedings continue in Florida. Tristan Tate has been held there since his arrest in Miami on 19 July, and a Thursday detention hearing will decide whether the brothers remain detained. - Advertisement - The filing puts 59 charges at the center of the dispute. The charges include rape, sex trafficking, and indecent images of a child, and prosecutors also pointed to allegations from four new accusers covering 2010-17, alongside earlier UK charges brought in 2025 involving three other accusers. Both sides filed new documents in the Southern District of Florida federal court. The British Embassy in Washington sent a request to the US Department of State to deny bail, keeping the issue in the same track as the extradition proceedings tied to the UK case. Prosecutors cite flight risk The Crown Prosecution Service says the brothers are a flight risk and said they would try to interfere with witnesses. Prosecutors argued in court filings that “Both Andrew and Tristan Tate have significant resources available to them, both in terms of money and in social media networks.” Prosecutors also wrote that “All of the complainants in this case are vulnerable and in fear of Andrew and Tristan Tate because of the violence used towards them – several of the complainants describe being assaulted and threatened with weapons – and because of the resources available to Andrew and Tristan Tate, and because of their propensity to intimidate vulnerable complainants.” - Advertisement - That is the point the judge will weigh on Thursday: whether those arguments justify keeping Tristan Tate and Andrew Tate jailed while extradition proceedings move forward, or whether bail changes their custody status before Britain seeks their return. UK charges and Romania path The new charges relate to allegations spanning 2010-17. The earlier 2025 UK case covers rape, bodily harm, human trafficking, and controlling prostitution for gain relating to three other accusers in the UK between 2012 and 2015. Police in Bedfordshire secured European arrest warrants in 2024 to have the brothers returned from Romania. The brothers moved to Romania in 2016, were arrested on sex charges in Romania in 2022, and later traveled to the US after travel restrictions in Romania were lifted in early 2025. For Tristan Tate, the immediate issue is custody in Florida. The Thursday detention hearing will decide whether he and Andrew Tate stay in jail while the extradition proceedings continue. https://nltimes.nl/2026/09/07/dutch-pm-j.text: Image Prime Minister Rob Jetten speaking during his regular weekly press conference. 28 Aug. 2026 - Credit: Algemeen Ministerie / RVD / Minister-President / YouTube - License: All Rights Reserved Politics the German Social Democrats AfD far-right Alternative for Germany CDU SPD FDP Die Linke Jetten Merz » More tags « Less tags Monday, 7 September 2026 - 16:10 Share this article: Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Dutch PM Jetten calls electoral win of far-right AfD in German state a "wake up call" The electoral victory of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) in the German state of Saxony-Anhalt is a “wake-up call” for politics in the neighboring country, said Dutch PM Rob Jetten. “The German voter is, of course, always right - including in German elections. At the same time, it is concerning that a party with extreme positions, which also contain pro-Russian sentiments, has performed so well,” the prime minister said during a working visit to the Zeeland town of Sluiskil. “What lessons do you draw from this, and how can you do better - including for the German voter?” German politicians and public officials must ask themselves after this electoral victory, according to the D66 PM said. Across Europe, the AfD’s victory has been met with concern. French and Polish ministers described it as a worrying signal. Former Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orbán, by contrast, called it a “great night for Germany and Europe” and congratulated the AfD. During the elections, the AfD fell just short of an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt. Preliminary results show that the party received 43.8 percent of the vote, which is as much as in the 2021 elections. Earlier forecasts had already indicated that the AfD would become the largest party in the eastern state. Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Christioan Democrats (CDU) finished second with 17.2 percent. The Social Democrats (SPD) received 9.3 percent, the Greens 8.9 percent, and Die Linke 8.6 percent. The far-left BSW party, with 5.3 percent, just cleared the electoral threshold and will therefore also enter the German parliament. Plattform Wahlen, a German nonprofit that monitors elections, reported that the Saxony-Anhalt election was marked by an “enourmous” amount of disinformation. Campaigns to spread fake news ahead of the vote reportedly launched from both inside Germany and from abroad. Several operations could allegedly be traced to Russian propoganda networks, said the platform’s founder Stefanie Schiffer. According to Schiffer, the smear campaigns especially target the CDU, SPD, FDP, and Die Linke candidates. In the meantime, Jetten was not the only leader to state their concerns. German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said freedom in the country is under pressure. He compared the danger posed by the far-right party to the Russian drones that have recently been appearing in German airspace. “Freedon in Germany is threatened from the outside by the Russian drones in our skies and the inside by Moscow's ideological low-flyers in our parliaments,” Dobrindt said at a political meeting in Bavaria. French Minister Roland Lescure told radio station RTL he was deeply concerned. “This shows the major challenge we face, with a populist wave spreading across the world that we have to stand up to.” Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski also voiced concern on a national radio station. The AfD has indicated that it now wants to press on and become the largest party nationwide as well. Co-leader Alice Weidel set a goal of winning at least 40 percent of the vote in the next federal election. “The CDU will never win another election,” Weidel said a day after the big win. Weidel continued by saying that the party will take the governing responsibility “seriously.” Saxony-Anhalt lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund also stressed that he wants to be a state premier for all residents if he is chosen to lead the government. That is not certain yet, because the AfD did not win an absolute majority. Siegmund said he wants a stable majority and therefore intends to talk with other parties. Four or five parties that won seats have ruled out working with the AfD because of its radical positions on issues including migration. Only the left-populist BSW did not.
